map.name: Attack Challenge
map.testedVersion: Full selected-artifact audit of Drive v1.1.2 across complete gameplay flow, six-arena source parity, shop/kit/inventory/economy writers, combat/death/respawn, retry/advance, terminal settlement, cleanup, and connection/reconnect paths. Source architecture supports six concurrent arena leases with one core ticking area per arena. Direct six-simultaneous-session runtime stress remains the narrow performance/runtime confirmation; no source-level two-arena blocker remains.

bugs.title: A last-second flag capture can still resolve the same level as both timeout and victory
bugs.problem: If the timer expires after a flag capture has already queued its victory callback, Attack can publish timeout/retry feedback and then accept the delayed victory for the same attempt. The late victory can also be scored with an invalid zero-duration attempt because timeout clears the attempt timestamps first.
bugs.expected: Each level attempt has exactly one terminal outcome. Once timeout wins terminal ownership, a queued flag-capture callback cannot settle victory, score the level, or publish level-complete feedback.
bugs.observed: FlagService.scoreFlag() queues endGame(arenaId, 'victory') one tick later. tickGameTimer() can call endGame(arenaId, 'timeout') first. The timeout retry branch clears startedAt and gameTimerEndsAt but leaves session.status active until the delayed retry. When the queued victory callback runs, endGame() has no terminal/reentrancy guard; hasGameTimerExpired() now returns false because gameTimerEndsAt is null, so victory is accepted. recordCompletedLevelScore() then sees cleared timing state, allowing the completion duration to collapse to zero before victory feedback/advance is scheduled.
reproduction: Reach an active Attack level while carrying the enemy flag near the capture zone.
Capture the flag at the same boundary where the game timer reaches zero, so the capture callback is queued while the timer expiry path also runs.
Observe whether 'Time's up' / retry feedback and level-complete/victory feedback both occur for the same attempt.
Check the stored/exported level duration and score for an impossible zero/near-zero successful attempt.
bugs.aiAnalysis: The timestamp check added in v1.1.2 only handles victory calls that still see the expired gameTimerEndsAt. It does not serialize terminal ownership. Timeout mutates the same session before the delayed FlagService victory callback executes, erasing the timestamp that the guard relies on. Because timeout schedules retry after 80 ticks while victory schedules advance after 60 ticks, victory can win the later transition while the player has already received timeout feedback. A terminal generation/outcome guard is required at endGame entry.

relevantCode.reason: FlagService.scoreFlag() defers the victory callback by one tick; tickGameTimer() independently calls timeout; endGame() lacks terminal ownership/reentrancy state and clears timing state in the timeout retry path.

bugs.suggestedFix: Claim one terminal outcome atomically per arena/attempt before mutating timers, score, feedback, or transitions. Ignore/cancel later terminal callbacks for that same attempt. Preserve the original terminal timestamp until the winning outcome has been fully settled.
mustPreserve: Normal flag captures before expiry still complete the level.
Normal timeout/wipe retry flow remains unchanged when it owns the terminal outcome.

bugs.title: Game-results export still identifies Attack Challenge as v1.1.0
bugs.problem: The v1.1.2 world and both pack manifests are version 1.1.2, but AttackGameResultsAdapter still exports map.version as 1.1.0, so result records can be attributed to the wrong build.
bugs.expected: Human-facing pack metadata and machine-readable game-results exports identify the same selected artifact version: v1.1.2.
bugs.observed: BP/RP manifests are [1,1,2], BP/RP language descriptions say 'Attack Challenge v1.1.2', and the Drive world is Attack Challenge v1.1.2.mcworld. AttackGameResultsAdapter still hardcodes ATTACK_MAP_INFO.version = '1.1.0'.
reproduction: Complete or force a score/export path in Attack Challenge v1.1.2.
Inspect the emitted Attack game-results payload.
Check map.version against the loaded world/pack version.
bugs.aiAnalysis: This is stale release metadata inside the results adapter, not a gameplay-state failure. It matters because exported QA/score records lose exact artifact provenance.
bugs.suggestedFix: Move Attack map version to one canonical release/version owner and consume it from pack/result presentation paths instead of maintaining a separate hardcoded results-adapter value.
mustPreserve: Existing score formula IDs and result schema.
Current v1.1.2 BP/RP manifest dependency parity.

bugs.title: A command-backed shop purchase consumes coins before delivery is confirmed
bugs.problem: The Speed Potion purchase removes its 12 coins before running the give command. If that command fails, the player loses the coins, receives no potion, and the shop still continues into its generic purchased-success message.
bugs.expected: A shop transaction either delivers the purchased item and charges the player once, or fails without consuming currency and without reporting success.
bugs.observed: ShopManager._executePurchase() calls consumeCoins() before player.runCommandAsync(itemDef.giveCommand). The catch path only logs and sends 'Failed to give item'; it does not refund the consumed coins or return before the generic 'Purchased ...' success message below the branch.
reproduction: Open the Attack shop and choose the Speed Potion purchase path.
Cause the command-backed item delivery to fail or become unavailable.
Check the player's coin balance and shop messages.
Observe whether 12 coins were consumed despite no potion being delivered and whether a generic purchase-success message still follows the failure.
bugs.aiAnalysis: The transaction commits currency before delivery and has no rollback. This is an atomicity defect isolated to command-backed shop items; normal ItemStack purchases add/drop the item after charging and do not use this failure branch.

relevantCode.reason: ShopManager._executePurchase() consumes coins before runCommandAsync(giveCommand), catches delivery failure without refund/return, then sends the generic purchase-success message.

bugs.suggestedFix: Make delivery and currency consumption one transaction: validate/deliver first and charge only on success, or refund and return on delivery failure. Never emit the generic purchase-success message after a failed delivery.
